question:
Let $\vec{p} = 3\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 5\hat{k}$ and $\vec{q} = 2\hat{i} + \hat{j} - 4\hat{k}$.

(a) Find a unit vector perpendicular to both $\vec{p}$ and $\vec{q}$.

(b) Find the area of the parallelogram formed by $\vec{p}$ and $\vec{q}$.

(c) Find a vector of magnitude 14 perpendicular to both $\vec{p}$ and $\vec{q}$.
explanation:
(a) A vector perpendicular to both $\vec{p}$ and $\vec{q}$ is given by their cross product:

$\vec{p} \times \vec{q} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 3 & -2 & 5 \\ 2 & 1 & -4 \end{vmatrix}$

$= \hat{i}[(-2)(-4) - (5)(1)] - \hat{j}[(3)(-4) - (5)(2)] + \hat{k}[(3)(1) - (-2)(2)]$

$= \hat{i}[8 - 5] - \hat{j}[-12 - 10] + \hat{k}[3 + 4]$

$= 3\hat{i} + 22\hat{j} + 7\hat{k}$

Magnitude: $|\vec{p} \times \vec{q}| = \sqrt{3^2 + 22^2 + 7^2} = \sqrt{9 + 484 + 49} = \sqrt{542}$

Unit vector: $\dfrac{3\hat{i} + 22\hat{j} + 7\hat{k}}{\sqrt{542}}$

(b) Area of parallelogram = $|\vec{p} \times \vec{q}| = \sqrt{542}$ square units

(c) A vector of magnitude 14 perpendicular to both $\vec{p}$ and $\vec{q}$ is:

$\vec{r} = 14 \cdot \dfrac{3\hat{i} + 22\hat{j} + 7\hat{k}}{\sqrt{542}} = \dfrac{42}{\sqrt{542}}\hat{i} + \dfrac{308}{\sqrt{542}}\hat{j} + \dfrac{98}{\sqrt{542}}\hat{k}$

Verification: $|\vec{r}| = 14 \cdot \dfrac{\sqrt{542}}{\sqrt{542}} = 14$
